findings.evidence: "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Replace or precede this paragraph with a short summary of what the stipend covers, how much it is worth, and who qualifies.
findings.violation: A section titled "Program Overview" never explains what the stipend covers or how the program works; it opens with budget-tracking and paper-copy logistics instead of an actual overview.

findings.evidence: "In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details the reviewer checks one at a time."
findings.fix: Use one consistent name for the benefit throughout, or explicitly state that "workspace stipend" and "home-office equipment stipend" refer to the same program.
findings.violation: The document has been discussing "the home-office equipment stipend" up to this point but here switches to "the workspace stipend" without saying whether this is the same benefit or a different one.

findings.evidence: "The workspace must sit inside the employee's primary residence for the stipend to apply. A workspace located in a shared coworking space does not qualify for the stipend under this section. A workspace used only occasionally for calls does not meet the bar the stipend policy sets."
findings.fix: Break this paragraph into a bulleted list of discrete workspace-eligibility conditions.
findings.location: Eligibility, third paragraph, workspace confirmation rules
findings.violation: Nine short, choppy sentences about workspace qualification rules are run together in a single dense paragraph, which makes the individual conditions hard to locate and compare.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the manager's approval form records approval already given or is a request awaiting the decision described in Approval Timeline.
findings.violation: It is unclear whether "the manager's approval form" documents approval already granted, which would make the review described in Approval Timeline redundant, or whether it is a request awaiting the manager's decision.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt... and the original purchase order before the review begins" versus "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount."
findings.fix: State explicitly whether employees are reimbursed after purchase or advanced funds before purchase, and use one consistent process description throughout.
findings.location: How to Apply, first paragraph, compared with Reimbursement Amounts, first paragraph
findings.violation: The document mixes two different funding models, a stipend advanced against a purchase order and a reimbursement paid after the fact against a receipt, without clarifying which one actually governs the program.

findings.evidence: "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: State explicitly what event the three-day period is measured from, such as the date the request was paused.
findings.violation: It is unclear what event starts the three-day count, since the preceding sentence only describes an indefinite pause rather than a specific start date.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: List the specific request types or dollar thresholds that require more than a photo receipt.
findings.violation: "Most requests" implies exceptions exist where a photo is not sufficient, but the document never says what those exceptions are or what additional documentation they require.

findings.evidence: "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount. Also, unused stipend amounts do not roll over to the next benefit year."
findings.fix: Add the stipend's dollar cap or coverage percentage to this section.
findings.violation: A section titled "Reimbursement Amounts" never states any actual dollar amount, cap, or coverage percentage for the stipend.

findings.evidence: "this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year"
findings.fix: Name the specific office, for example the benefits team, that performs the photo check.
findings.violation: "This office" has no clear antecedent in the sentence or the paragraph; no specific office was named immediately before this reference.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk..."
findings.fix: Split this into a base rule sentence stating one device per category per employee, followed by a clearly labeled exception sentence describing when a second device in the same category is permitted.
findings.violation: The sentence states a one-device-per-category limit and then immediately describes an exception permitting a second device in the same category, but the run-on sentence structure buries the contradiction between the stated limit and its exception.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Rewrite this section in the same third-person voice used throughout the rest of the document.
findings.violation: The document uses third-person voice, "employees," "the applicant," "the requester," everywhere else, but this section abruptly switches to second-person "you" without explanation.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form."
findings.fix: Either define "stipend item" explicitly, or rename this section to describe the process it actually covers.
findings.violation: A section titled "Terminology Notes" never defines what a "stipend item" is or how it differs from "the stipend"; it describes a process instead of defining any term.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Reconcile the steps listed here with the full process described in How to Apply, or remove this section if it duplicates that one.
findings.violation: This section lists only two steps, but How to Apply earlier requires submitting a manager's approval form and purchase order and reviewing a confirmation summary; the two step lists are inconsistent with each other.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Replace this section with content describing actual special-case scenarios, or remove the section.
findings.violation: This text is nearly identical to the opening paragraph of Program Overview, with "benefits team" swapped for "finance liaison," and describes no actual special case despite the section heading.

findings.evidence: "The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Define "repeat request" and describe what the escalation process involves.
findings.violation: "Repeat requests" is never defined anywhere in the document, so it is unclear what qualifies as a repeat request or what the automatic escalation actually does.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Replace this section with actual contact information for questions and a description of how policy updates are communicated.
findings.violation: This closing section is nearly identical to the Program Overview paragraph and provides no way to ask questions or find policy updates, despite its heading.
